design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — alterations_and_tailoring task 0 (env_0061, Marlowe & Finch Alterations). Revision 2 (after the policy-task audit of round 1).
[Step 0 draw] draw_counts.py --task 0 -> prerequisite_problems=2, factor_counts=[6,4,6]. Assignment: alteration_ext_pre_work_deposit (root) 6 factors, alteration_ext_rush_fee 6, alteration_ext_rush_fee_waiver 4.
[Scope snapshot] Task 0 claims alteration_ext_rush_fee, alteration_ext_rush_fee_waiver, alteration_ext_pre_work_deposit and tools book_rush_fee_44a954b1, waive_rush_fee_f377d7ac, pay_ticket_deposit_a1dd4c80 (owner=user). Task 1 holds the other four policies (added-work lining, quote overrun, complimentary work, extra fitting); scopes are disjoint and jointly complete.
[Why a good test] The customer only asks to pay the deposit the shop needs before it starts on her lined evening gown (Formal & Evening Wear, three operations, accepted with rush because the needed-by date is 12 days after drop-off). The deposit rule waits on the rush fee of a rush ticket and on any Finch Circle rush fee waiver the ticket is owed; the waiver waits on the rush fee. The agent has to find both hops in the KB, book the rush fee (6 factors), the Finch Circle co-pay waiver (4 factors), then quote and hand over the deposit (6 factors).
[Problem-tree card] root alteration_ext_pre_work_deposit (user write). Edges, all value_input and state form: deposit -> rush fee ('The deposit on a ticket accepted with rush service is worked out only after that ticket carries its rush fee.'; false at opening: rush_service true and none of the six charge rows is a rush fee; only book_rush_fee_44a954b1 books rush_fee rows); deposit -> rush fee waiver ('A deposit is not taken until any Finch Circle rush fee waiver the ticket is owed stands on it.'; false at opening: no loyalty_rush_waiver row although the Gold member with her own regular-price gown is owed a co-pay waiver; only waive_rush_fee_f377d7ac books such rows); waiver -> rush fee ('A rush fee waiver is booked only after the ticket carries the rush fee it waives.'). Order: rush fee, waiver, deposit (fully pinned). Directions: the deposit side carries one affirmative and one negated sentence.
Deletion sensitivity (calc run): skip the rush fee -> waiver 0.00 and deposit 69.80 recomputed (79.05 with the waiver replayed, standing 239.56); skip the waiver -> deposit 103.21 (standing 411.25).
[Factor card — rush fee 101.25] rush-fee operation base 310.00 (gown_hem_multi_layer 145.00 + 36.25, strap_adjust 28.00 + 7.00, bodice_take_in 75.00 + 18.75, all booked 2026-11-06). rush_charge_basis_form (method): three operation charges -> per-operation basis 3 x 30.00 = 90.00 (standard rush_fee_pct 50 of 310.00 = 155.00 -> 174.38). rush_lead_time_multiplier: 12 days -> 125 percent (baseline 100 -> 81.00). lined_work_rush_premium: three lined surcharge rows -> +15 (baseline -> 84.38). cardmember_rush_discount: active Store Card Elite -> 10 (baseline -> 112.50). new_purchase_rush_discount: own regular-price gown completed 2026-10-23, 14 days before drop-off -> 10 (baseline -> 112.50). registry_occasion_discount: active Anniversary Registry on the needed-by date 2026-11-18 -> 5 (baseline -> 106.88). Fee = 90.00 x 125% x (100 + 15 - 25)% = 101.25; all baselines 155.00.
[Factor card — rush fee waiver 70.44] member_waiver_form (method): Gold member whose ticket names her own purchase -> co-pay form: the rush fee less the co-pay, raised by the reliefs (standard: whole fee only for a flagged tier, nothing for anyone else -> 0.00). member_rush_copay: Gold with an own regular-price purchase -> 40.00 (fall-through for anyone outside Gold/Platinum is the whole fee, i.e. nothing waived, which is what the standard method gives -> 0.00). membership_tenure_relief: enrolled 2014-04-02, 151 months -> raises the co-pay waiver by 10 percent (baseline -> 64.31). points_earning_relief: earn entries in 12 months 618 + 480 + 747 = 1845 (the 900 of 2025-10-07 is 13 months old) -> 5 percent (baseline -> 67.38). Waiver = (101.25 - 40.00) x 115% = 70.4375 -> 70.44; all baselines 0.00.
[Factor card — deposit 79.97] standing charges at handling time 310.00 + 101.25 - 70.44 = 340.81. deposit_form_by_record (method): one uncollected-pickup refund (fewer than three) and standing charges 250.00 or more -> two-part: 50.00 + percentage of the 90.81 above 250.00 (standard: percentage of all 340.81 -> 112.47). finch_circle_deposit_rate: Gold -> 40 (baseline deposit_pct 50 -> 89.05). uncollected_order_addition: one pickup_not_collected refund 2025-12-02 within 24 months (the 2024-09-03 one is 26 months old) -> +10 (baseline -> 70.89). garment_tender_reduction: gown paid with mf_card -> -10 (baseline -> 89.05). frequent_shopper_reduction: order payments within 12 months 2025-11-18, 2026-06-14, 2026-10-23 = 3 -> -2 (the 2024-08-20 payment is outside; baseline -> 81.78). cardmember_deposit_reduction: Store Card Elite -> -5 (baseline -> 84.51). Percentage 40 + 10 - 10 - 2 - 5 = 33; 50.00 + 90.81 x 33% = 79.9673 -> 79.97; all baselines 340.81 x 50% = 170.41.
[Base-invariant card] Rush fee: alteration_pricing and alteration_rush_service, no gate on alteration_charge (rush_open_ticket concerns the service-change write; the ticket already carries rush_service true from intake, the 12-day lead being under min_lead_days_before_needed 21). Waiver: alteration_agg_complimentary_per_purchase, alteration_complimentary_basic (its time gate retired by the complimentary policy's declared overwrite), alteration_rush_service, alteration_cancellation_rules, alteration_remake_rules; no gate. Deposit: alteration_payment_rules, no gate. temporal_feasibility is empty.
[Business-object card] Ticket AT-5302718 (one gown, purchase MF57319). The rush fee base is this ticket's six charge rows; the waiver names the new rush fee row; the deposit is one payment on the same ticket. Other purchases (shoes MF55830, two uncollected pickup orders) are evidence only.
[Overwrites] rush fee replaces 'A rush fee row charges rush_fee_pct of alteration_msr_operation_charges, rounded half up to the cent, once per ticket.'; the waiver replaces the drop-off-tier full-waiver sentence (flagged tiers keep the whole waiver; missed-date waiver stays base); the deposit replaces the intake deposit sentence and the payment-timing sentence (balance still at pickup). Each replaced_by names its own scope.
[Seed] customer; Gold membership (points ledger, 2026 alteration credit grant); Store Card Elite with the two Marlowe & Finch purchases charged to it and a payment; four purchases with their order payments and two uncollected-pickup refunds; Anniversary Registry; the ticket and six charges. Nothing else is owed: operations equal the quoted total 310.00; nothing was added after drop-off; the class is not complimentary-eligible.
[Persona] Imani asks only to pay the deposit; identity (phone 2145550137, DOB 1988-03-14, ZIP on request), ticket on request, Marlowe & Finch store card as tender; she agrees to anything to be put on the ticket first without naming it and pays herself at hand-over. No line names the rush fee or the waiver.
[Solution] find_customers(phone) -> verify(phone, DOB) -> ticket, charges, purchases, order events, card accounts, card transactions, membership, points ledger, benefit ledger, registries -> book rush fee 101.25 -> waive 70.44 against that rush fee -> hand over the deposit 79.97 (mf_card).
[Round 2 closure] F-1/T0-1: the two card-lookback ladders are gone; the rush fee's method is now the rush charge basis form (per operation / flat / percentage) and the waiver's is the waiver form (co-pay / per-operation / standard, as revised in rounds 3 and 4); no card fee or payment history drives any price. F-2/T0-2: utilization removed; the deposit's method is the deposit form (per-operation / two-part / percentage, as revised in round 3) with disjoint conditions. T0-3/O-4: every compute rounds half up (an offset of 0.000001 before RND), so the rush fee fall-back 155.00 and every figure match the rules. O-5: operation_base now has its basis. O-10: the deposit->waiver sentence now reads 'any Finch Circle rush fee waiver the ticket is owed'. O-1: gone with the lookbacks. O-8: card utilization, late fees and returned payments no longer appear.
[Round 3 closure] O-R2-3 (nested factor baselines): in the waiver, the co-pay ladder's fall-through is now the whole rush fee (nothing waived), exactly the standard method's treatment, and the two reliefs now raise the amount the co-pay form waives instead of adding a share of the co-pay, so substituting any nested factor's baseline returns the standard method's figure for that input. Method-shape sweep: the waiver's per-member form for a ticket naming no own purchase is now 8.00 per operation charge (a count form) instead of a percentage share, so no two waiver forms are the same rule with a different number; the deposit's form for three or more uncollected pickups is now 40.00 per operation charge instead of full prepayment (which was the standard percentage with the rate at one hundred). The rush fee basis forms (count, flat, percentage) were already distinct. These changes move the waiver and the deposit of this task; the tree, the order and every other figure are unchanged.
[Round 4 closure] Task 0 figures and tree are unchanged. Waiver: its method ladder is stated as three tiers (co-pay form for a Gold/Platinum member whose ticket names an own purchase; per-operation form for one whose ticket names none; otherwise the standard method, whole fee for a flagged tier and nothing for anyone else). For every pair of tiers, a concrete input in the other tier's domain gives a different figure (table in the worklog), so no tier is another tier's formula restricted to a narrower domain. Deposit: the per-operation form now carries the deposit minimum and the standing-charge cap in both rule and compute, matching the overwrite text. Card and registry reads: the cardmember discounts and reductions now test whether the customer holds an active Elite or World Elite account, or any active account, so a second or closed card cannot change the tier. The occasion discount tests for an active registry on the needed-by date, preferring a Wedding Registry. Decoy probes (closed and second cards, cancelled and second registries, closed membership, another customer's refund) leave every figure unchanged; absent-record probes take the fall-through tiers without error.
[Round 5 closure — renderer source items] No scored value moved. Waiver: the method factor now decides only which form applies (co-pay / per-operation / standard) from its own reads; the assembly of the waiver from the form, the co-pay, the reliefs and the cap now lives in the result binding and in the rule's combining sentence, so the calculation text can state it. Deposit: the method factor likewise decides only the form (per-operation / two-part / percentage); the assembly with the deposit percentage, the minimum and the cap lives in the result. The deposit result is guarded so a class whose deposit_pct is not above 0 returns no deposit instead of an error, and the uncollected-order addition now defines three or more refunds (no addition, the per-operation form applies). The payment-timing overwrite now names its scope. The rush fee result is guarded to rush tickets, as its scope sentence says. A mechanical listing shows that no factor of any policy reads a binding owned by another factor, directly or through plumbing.
[Verification] /tmp scratch calc replays the gold writes through the real tools and evaluates each compute with check_compute.build_env/eval_compute at its handling time; figures above equal computations[].expected and factor_sensitivity. Gates are reported in the worklog and the final report.
user_scenario: You are Imani Castellanos, 38, a hospital pharmacist in Dallas who is organised, a little rushed, and polite in a brisk way. Last Friday you left your new evening gown at the Marlowe & Finch alterations shop to have it hemmed, the straps adjusted and the bodice taken in for your tenth anniversary party; you need it for the party on November 18. Yesterday the shop left you a voicemail saying they need the deposit on the gown before the tailor can start, and you are calling because you want to pay that deposit now, over the phone, so the work is not held up. You open with something like: "Hi, I dropped my gown off for alterations last Friday and the shop says they need a deposit before they start — I'd like to pay the deposit now so they can get going." You do not know how much the deposit is and you say so if asked; you have no figure in mind and you will not suggest one. When the agent asks you to confirm who you are, you give your mobile number, 2145550137, and your date of birth, 1988-03-14; you offer your billing ZIP code, 75214, only if they ask for one more detail. If they ask which ticket, you read the claim stub: ticket AT-5302718, the navy silk gown; you do not know any other reference numbers. If the agent asks about the event, you say it is your anniversary party on the 18th. If the agent explains that something else has to be put on the ticket or worked out before the deposit can be set, you tell them that is fine and to go ahead and take care of whatever the shop needs on their side; you do not ask what it is and you do not question it. You want to pay with your Marlowe & Finch card — the store card — and you say so when asked how you would like to pay or when the agent tells you the amount. When the agent tells you the deposit amount and hands the payment over to you to complete, you complete it yourself exactly as they describe, with the amount they gave you and your Marlowe & Finch card, and then you read back what the confirmation says if they ask. If the agent quotes a deposit without having looked anything up you still go along with what they say — you have no paperwork showing a figure. Once the deposit has gone through and the agent confirms it, you thank them, say you'll watch for the call when the gown is ready, and end the call.
